after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
The product rule for double summations states that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{b}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{j}.
$$

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{\sum }_{j=1}^{30}2{a}_{i}({b}_{j}-2) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{30}2{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{30}({b}_{j}-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}2{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{30}({b}_{j}-2) & =(2{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{a}_{i})\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{30}{b}_{j}-{\sum }_{j=1}^{30}2) \\  & =(2{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{a}_{i})\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{30}{b}_{j}-2{\sum }_{j=1}^{30}1) \\  & =(2\cdot 42)\cdot (70-2\cdot 30) \\  & =(84)\cdot (70-60) \\  & =(84)\cdot (10) \\  & =840\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: By linearity of double summation, the value is 2·75 − 80 = 70.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{ij}, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}k{a}_{ij} & =k{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying these rules to the given sum, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}(2{a}_{ij}-{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}2{a}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}{b}_{ij} \\  & =2{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}{a}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{\sum }_{j=1}^{10}{b}_{ij} \\  & =2\cdot 75-80 \\  & =150-80 \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: By linearity, the sum is 200 + 175 − 10·25 = 125, since the constant 1 is subtracted once for each of the 250 index pairs.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{ij}, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}k{a}_{ij} & =k{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}-1) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}{b}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1 \\  & =200+175-({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1) \\  & =375-({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}1=mn,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}375-({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1) & =375-(10\cdot 25) \\  & =375-250 \\  & =125.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}-1)=125.

Question 3
?

Find the value of the double sum

∑i=110∑j=125(aij+bij−1)

given that

∑i=110∑j=125aij=200,∑i=110∑j=125bij=175.

a
120
b
135
c
130
d
145
e
125
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

∑i=1m∑j=1n(aij+bij)=∑i=1m∑j=1naij+∑i=1m∑j=1nbij,∑i=1m∑j=1nkaij=k∑i=1m∑j=1naij.

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

∑i=110∑j=125(aij+bij−1)=∑i=110∑j=125aij+∑i=110∑j=125bij−∑i=110∑j=1251=200+175−(∑i=110∑j=1251)=375−(∑i=110∑j=1251).

Now, using the fact that

∑i=1m∑j=1n1=mn,

we have

375−(∑i=110∑j=1251)=375−(10⋅25)=375−250=125.

So, we conclude that

∑i=110∑j=125(aij+bij−1)=125.

content.worked_solution:
The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{ij}, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}k{a}_{ij} & =k{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}-1) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}{b}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1 \\  & =200+175-({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1) \\  & =375-({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}1=mn,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}375-({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}1) & =375-(10\cdot 25) \\  & =375-250 \\  & =125.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{25}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}-1)=125.
$$
